part.text: I need to close the previous `<li>` when a new list item line starts — the original did that at the newline. Fixing:

All 17 tests pass and `go vet` is clean. ## What I did The spec in `.docs/instructions.md` is a refactoring exercise: the original `Render` in `markdown.go` walked the input one byte at a time, juggling four intertwined pieces of state (`header`, `list`, `listOpened`, and a cryptic `he` flag) with special-case hacks (e.g. emitting a literal `"# "` when a hash appears mid-header, and using `strings.LastIndex` comparisons to detect the end of a list). I rewrote it as a line-oriented parser, since every construct in this exercise is line-based: - **`renderEmphasis`** — extracts the up-front `__`/`_` → ``/`` substitution, with a comment explaining why bold must be replaced before italic (so `__` isn't consumed as two single underscores). Behavior is unchanged. - **`headerLevel`** — recognizes `#`–`######` followed by a space; 7+ hashes falls through to paragraph rendering (matching the "h7 is a paragraph" test). - **`listItem`** — recognizes `* ` at the start of a line. - **`Render`** — splits the input into lines and dispatches each to those helpers, tracking only two booleans: `inList` and `inParagraph`. A new list item closes the previous `
  • `; a non-list line closes the whole list; plain text opens/closes a `

    ` block. The refactoring rationale is documented in the `Render` doc comment, as the instructions suggested. No changes to `markdown_test.go`, `cases_test.go`, or any other file.
